places.name: Volume
places.description: A former woodworker's shop turned café-bar on Florence's liveliest student piazza, with live music, art on the shelves and crowds spilling onto the square. Grab a ~€5-6 spritz that comes with free snacks and join the Santo Spirito evening scene. It's the default meeting point for students on the Oltrarno side.
places.reviewSummary: Named repeatedly across local and student guides as Florence's most-loved budget aperitivo, with consistently warm reviews of staff, music and prices.

quotes.text: Prices at Café Volume remain affordable without sacrificing quality.
Where young professionals and students gather for strong cocktails and live music. Most cocktails are 9 euro and excellent.

places.name: Bulli e Balene
places.description: A tiny Venetian-style bacaro in the Oltrarno serving spritz and 'ombra' wine for around €4.50 with €1-2 cicchetti toasts. Order a tray of cicchetti and drink standing in the pretty lane near Piazza della Passera. One of the cheapest quality aperitivo runs in the center.
places.reviewSummary: Local guides single it out as exceptional value for spritz plus cicchetti in an otherwise pricey area.

quotes.text: Serves up exceptionally budget friendly Spritz and ombra for around 4.50 euro.

places.name: Enoteca alla Sosta dei Papi
places.description: A hole-in-the-wall enoteca in Sant'Ambrogio pouring Tuscan wine by the glass (and by the liter, straight from barrels) at student prices, with coccoli and crostini to snack on. The crowd of locals and students spills onto Borgo la Croce every evening. The perfect start to a Sant'Ambrogio bar crawl.
places.reviewSummary: Repeatedly cited by locals and students as the best cheap wine hang in Florence; reviewers marvel at the prices.

quotes.text: Sample local Tuscan wines on a dime... by the glass or by the liter from barrels.
The prices are amazingly cheap... a bottle of house red, house white and two glasses of red for 13 euro.

places.name: Amblé
places.description: A vintage-furniture café-bar hidden in a courtyard steps from Ponte Vecchio, where every one of its 15+ spritz variations costs €7. Mismatched flea-market chairs, good panini and a young international crowd. Feels like a secret even though it's in the most touristy corner of town.
places.reviewSummary: Praised for keeping flat, honest prices and a cool design-shop vibe despite a prime Ponte Vecchio location.

quotes.text: Choose from over 15 different Spritz variations, all for 7 euro.

places.name: Le Volpi e l'Uva
places.description: A serious little wine bar tucked behind Ponte Vecchio pouring small-producer wines by the glass with crostini, cheeses and cured meats. A €10-15 glass-plus-plate here beats most sit-down dinners. Where students bring visiting parents to look like they know Florence.
places.reviewSummary: A fixture on every quality-for-price aperitivo list; loved for expert pours at fair prices in a tourist-free pocket.

quotes.text: Small plate of meats & cheeses and a glass of wine for 10-15 euro.

places.name: Caffetteria delle Oblate
places.address: Via dell'Oriuolo 24 (Biblioteca delle Oblate, top floor), 50122 Firenze
places.description: The rooftop café of the Oblate public library, with a straight-on terrace view of Brunelleschi's dome that would cost triple anywhere else. Its apericena buffet lets you turn one cheap drink into dinner while studying or people-watching with Florentine students. The best view-per-euro ratio in the city.
places.reviewSummary: Beloved by local and international students alike for a budget apericena directly facing the Duomo.

quotes.text: The Oblate Library upstairs student cafe is the best spot for apericena with a view in Florence.

places.name: Santarosa Bistrot
places.description: A garden bistrot built into the old city walls in San Frediano, with plants everywhere, good cocktails and aperitivo snacks under the trees. Berlin-café energy by day, packed young-Florentine scene by night. Worth the walk west along the Arno for golden-hour drinks.
places.reviewSummary: A consistent local-crowd favorite for garden aperitivo; slightly pricier drinks but the setting wins reviewers over.

quotes.text: Popular among families in the morning and students and professionals in the evening, resembling a Berlin vibe more than San Frediano.

places.name: La Cité Libreria Café
places.description: A bookshop-café-bar hybrid in San Frediano with mezzanine seating, cheap glasses of wine and an evening program of jazz, folk and open-mic nights. Study here in the afternoon and stay for live music with a local crowd. The anti-American-pub option for a low-key night.
places.reviewSummary: A long-running Oltrarno institution that locals and study-abroad blogs both recommend for live music without tourist pricing.

quotes.text: Lively student haunts around Sant'Ambrogio and the Oltrarno offer a casual aperitivo crawl from bar to bar.

places.name: The Lion's Fountain
places.description: The unofficial living room of American study-abroad Florence: an Irish pub plastered with college banners and business cards on Piazza San Pier Maggiore. Monday is Dollar Night (pay in USD), Wednesday is college night, Thursday karaoke. You will run into someone from your program here, guaranteed.
places.reviewSummary: The single most-mentioned bar in study-abroad guides; scores for atmosphere and deals rather than craft.

quotes.text: Dollar Night: 6 of them or 5 euros for your choice of draft beer and the shot of your choosing.
They allow you to bring food from outside and eat alongside your beer.

places.name: Red Garter
places.description: A 1962-vintage American-style steakhouse-bar that functions as study-abroad HQ on Via de' Benci: sports on the screens, a dance floor, and a full karaoke stage with a live guitarist. Come for beer pong and NFL games, stay for the chaos after midnight. Touristy, but a rite of passage.
places.reviewSummary: Universally known and reliably fun for the student crowd, though reviewers agree it's an American bubble rather than an Italian night out.

quotes.text: Florence's unofficial study abroad headquarters... the biggest appeal is the karaoke on a full-blown stage with a live guitar player.

places.name: Kikuya Pub
places.description: A dark English-style pub near Santa Croce famous for its house Dragoon beer at a fearsome 10% ABV and Tuesday/Thursday sticker nights where beer caps win free rounds and t-shirts. Mixed Italian and international crowd, cheap pints, good burgers. A Via de' Benci bar-crawl anchor since the 90s.
places.reviewSummary: A student-guide staple for decades; scores on deals and energy, with the Dragoon beer its signature draw.

quotes.text: Buy any beer (Dragoon's are the best!) and underneath will be a sticker you peel off for the chance to win beers, shots, t-shirts, hats.
Known among Italians and foreigners for their Dragoon Beer which has an incredible 10% alcohol content.

places.name: Shot Café
places.description: A neon-lit dive near the Duomo that study-abroad students treat as the official pregame: trays of flavored shots, pitchers of mixed drinks and happy-hour prices most of the night. Loud, sticky and cheerfully unpretentious. Nobody's first choice for a quiet drink, everybody's first stop before the club.
places.reviewSummary: Wins on price and party energy across student guides; drink quality is beside the point.

quotes.text: One of the cheapest bars in Florence, offering shot trays, large mixed-drink pitchers, and varied shot options.

places.name: Monkey Bar
places.description: A scruffy, well-loved bar off Sant'Ambrogio where Italian university students outnumber Americans and drinks stay cheap all night. Foosball, spritzes, and a crowd that spills onto the sidewalk in warm months. Go here to actually meet Florentines your age.
places.reviewSummary: Recommended in student guides precisely because it draws more locals than study-abroad crowds while keeping dive-bar prices.

quotes.text: Attracts more locals than American students; a cultural experience.

places.name: The Box Bar
places.description: A no-sign, no-frills neighborhood bar on Borgo Pinti with prices that feel like a typo: €1 appetizers, €1.50 wine, €2.50 beer, €3.50 Aperol spritz. Blink and you'll walk past it; the regulars like it that way. The cheapest legitimate drink in the historic center.
places.reviewSummary: A Gen-Z budget-guide find prized for rock-bottom prices and a genuine local dive atmosphere; zero polish by design.

quotes.text: It's conveniently located on Via Borgo Pinti, but you might miss it since there's no sign outside.

places.name: Mad Souls & Spirits
places.description: San Frediano's irreverent craft cocktail bar, where two of Italy's best-known bartenders serve seriously built drinks from about €8 with zero speakeasy attitude and free snacks on the counter. The blackboard menu changes constantly and the room is always buzzing. The best drink-per-euro cocktail in Florence.
places.reviewSummary: Appears on every credible Florence cocktail list while staying walk-in casual and affordable, a rare combination reviewers keep noting.

quotes.text: No reservations or secret codes required - just walk in and enjoy expertly crafted cocktails.
The place, like its prices, is easy and accessible.

places.name: Il Santino
places.description: A postage-stamp wine bar in the Oltrarno with four tables, superb cheeses and cured meats, and well-priced glasses of Tuscan wine. The crowd drinks on the street outside in classic Florentine fashion. Ideal for an aperitivo that feels grown-up without a grown-up bill.
places.reviewSummary: Small-format wine bar loved by locals and food writers alike for quality far above its price point.

quotes.text: Though it has only four tables... Il Santino is blessed with a big wine list and superior cheeses, cured meats, and other delicacies to match.

places.name: All'Antico Vinaio
places.description: The world's most famous sandwich shop: enormous schiacciata stuffed with sbriciolona, truffle cream, pecorino and pistachio spreads for around €7-9. The line down Via dei Neri is part of the experience; multiple storefronts on the same street keep it moving. Iconic first-week-of-the-semester food.
places.reviewSummary: Earns near-universal acclaim and 30,000+ reviews; a few locals call it hyped, but the quality-to-price ratio still wins.

quotes.text: Earned the title 'Home of the World's Best Sandwiches' from Saveur... crowds willing to queue for 45 minutes to an hour.

places.name: Semel
places.description: A closet-sized sandwich counter opposite Sant'Ambrogio market where the owner invents small gourmet panini — think anchovy with orange, or stewed boar — for a few euros each. No seats, just a shelf and a glass of wine. The connoisseur's answer to the All'Antico Vinaio line.
places.reviewSummary: Food writers' consistent pick for the most creative cheap panino in Florence, with a devoted local following.

quotes.text: Tuscan cooked specialties stuffed in a roll.

places.name: I Due Fratellini
places.description: A literal hole in the wall (since 1875) two blocks from the Duomo serving ~30 numbered panini and glasses of Chianti you rest on a wooden ledge. Sandwich plus wine runs well under €10. Order the finocchiona with pecorino and eat standing in the street like generations before you.
places.reviewSummary: A 150-year-old institution that guides love for the ritual as much as the sandwich; fast, cheap and central.

quotes.text: Super hole in the wall experience.

places.name: Da Nerbone
places.address: Mercato Centrale (ground floor), Piazza del Mercato Centrale, 50123 Firenze
places.description: The grand old counter of the Mercato Centrale, serving lampredotto and bollito (boiled beef) sandwiches dunked in broth since 1872. Order 'bagnato con salsa verde' and eat at the marble tables. The classic gateway into Florence's offal street-food tradition.
places.reviewSummary: In every guide and still worth it: reviewers across sources call the lunchtime queue justified by the broth-soaked bollito.

quotes.text: The grand old name in Florentine boiled meat sandwiches... there's almost always a queue at lunchtime, and it's worth it.

places.name: Tripperia Pollini (Sergio Pollini)
places.description: The Sant'Ambrogio lampredotto stand where actual market shoppers eat lunch: a €4-5 tripe sandwich with salsa verde and a plastic cup of wine. Quieter and arguably better-brothed than the famous central carts. Peak cheap-and-real Florence.
places.reviewSummary: Named by local food press as having some of the best broth in the city, with a genuinely local clientele.

quotes.text: The counter where the people who actually shop at Sant'Ambrogio have their lunch... some of the best broth in the city.

places.name: Il Trippaio del Porcellino
places.description: The most central lampredotto cart, parked beside the bronze boar of the Mercato Nuovo. A fast-moving lunch line of office workers and brave students grabbing tripe sandwiches between classes. Rub the Porcellino's snout for luck, then order 'bagnato'.
places.reviewSummary: Consistently rated excellent and the easiest lampredotto to reach from anywhere in the center.

quotes.text: Busy, fast moving lunchtime queue, generally excellent.

places.name: Focacceria Pugi
places.description: The legendary schiacciata bakery on Piazza San Marco, steps from the Accademia and half the study-abroad classrooms in town. Slabs of oily, salty schiacciata — plain or stuffed — sold by weight for pocket change. The default between-class snack since 1924.
places.reviewSummary: Routinely called the best schiacciata in town and perfectly placed for students; cheap, fast and reliably great.

quotes.text: One of the best bakeries for schiacciata in town.

places.name: Trattoria Mario
places.description: A lunch-only, cash-friendly, shared-table trattoria behind the Mercato Centrale run by the same family since 1953. Handwritten daily menu, ribollita and pasta for single digits, and famously cheap grilled steak. Arrive before noon or accept the queue — either way it's the best-value sit-down meal in Florence.
places.reviewSummary: Legendary status confirmed across every source: genuine Florentine cooking at the lowest prices in town, hence the daily line.

quotes.text: Genuine Florentine cooking at the lowest prices in town... a boneless grilled steak for 12 euros plus a glass of red wine, totaling 14 euros.

places.name: Trattoria da Rocco
places.address: Inside Mercato di Sant'Ambrogio, Piazza Ghiberti, 50122 Firenze
places.description: A booth-seating trattoria inside the Sant'Ambrogio market hall where primi run €5-6 and a full lunch with wine stays under €15. Home-style Florentine plates — pasta al ragù, polpette, roast meats — served at market speed. The single best cheap sit-down lunch trick students learn.
places.reviewSummary: A top pick in budget dining guides for quality home cooking at market-stall prices.

quotes.text: Dirt cheap and quality home-style Florentine fare - top pick.

places.name: Gustapizza
places.description: The Oltrarno pizzeria that every study-abroad student learns in week one: proper Neapolitan-style pies from about €6-9, heart-shaped if you ask nicely, eaten in the tiny room or carried to Piazza Santo Spirito. The line out the door at 7pm is all students. Cheap, fast and genuinely good.
places.reviewSummary: The consensus student pizza in Florence: long lines, soft-dough pies and prices that fit a student budget.

quotes.text: A popular pizzeria in Florence with long lines and soft dough pies.

places.name: Trattoria Sabatino
places.description: A fluorescent-lit, family-run time capsule just outside Porta San Frediano where handwritten menus list primi around €5 and secondi under €10. No frills, no tourists, no reservations — just honest Florentine home cooking. Where Oltrarno locals and in-the-know students eat when rent is due.
places.reviewSummary: Beloved across local guides as the realest cheap trattoria left in Florence; simplicity is the entire point.

quotes.text: Truly simple, non-fussy food.

places.name: L'Antica Mescita San Niccolò
places.description: A rustic osteria partly set in an 11th-century crypt in the San Niccolò bar district, serving ribollita, peposo and big plates of Tuscan comfort food at low prices. Perfectly placed for dinner before drinks in Piazza Poggi or the climb to Piazzale Michelangelo. Cozy, candlelit and cheap.
places.reviewSummary: Budget guides recommend it for no-frills Tuscan classics in one of the best evening neighborhoods.

quotes.text: No-frills dirt cheap Tuscan fare in a rustic atmosphere.

places.name: Space Club
places.description: The biggest club in the historic center: two floors, international DJs, a karaoke area and a crowd that's heavily study-abroad on weekends. Cover usually includes a drink; it goes late Tuesday through Saturday. The default 'everyone's going to Space' night out.
places.reviewSummary: The most consistently named club in student guides; big, reliable fun even if drinks inside add up.

quotes.text: Florence's biggest club of them all... multiple floors, dancers everywhere, some of the world's biggest DJ's.
The biggest club in the historic centre, with two dance floors... attracts people from all over the world.

places.name: YAB
places.description: Florence's historic basement club behind Palazzo Strozzi, running since 1974. Monday night ('SMOOVE') is the institution — hip-hop, Afrobeats and reggaeton with a mixed Italian and international student crowd. Dress a little better than for the pubs and expect a cover with drink.
places.reviewSummary: The Monday-night institution of Florence nightlife, still going strong in 2026 with an international student following.

quotes.text: SMOOVE every Monday night... the go-to for the international crowd looking for a consistent nightlife experience.

places.name: Blob Club
places.description: A scruffy two-level members-style club behind Palazzo Vecchio with no cover, cheap drinks and a dance floor that fills after the pubs close. Upstairs sofas, downstairs DJ, zero pretension. The budget alternative when you want to dance without paying club cover.
places.reviewSummary: Student guides recommend it exactly for the no-cover, cheap-drinks formula; divey but dependable.

quotes.text: No cover charge; dancing venue for budget-conscious visitors.

places.name: Club TwentyOne
places.description: A compact basement club between the Duomo and Piazza della Signoria with good DJs and free entry on student-heavy weeknights. Less overwhelming than Space, more of a dance-floor-first room. Solid Wednesday option in the city center.
places.reviewSummary: A student-guide regular for free-entry midweek nights with better-than-expected DJs.

quotes.text: Smaller club with no cover on Wednesdays; features quality DJs.

places.name: Gelateria della Passera
places.description: A tiny all-natural gelateria on the adorable Piazza della Passera in the Oltrarno, churning seasonal flavors like fig, prickly pear and superb pistachio from a kitchen right behind the counter. Small scoops, real fruit, fair prices. Combine with an evening drink on the piazza.
places.reviewSummary: A quality-first hidden gem that food writers and gelato obsessives consistently rank among Florence's very best.

quotes.text: A hidden gem known for its exceptional gelato quality and unique flavors... made with the freshest seasonal ingredients.

places.name: Gelateria La Carraia
places.description: The student favorite at the foot of Ponte alla Carraia: huge creamy scoops, a famous €1 mini-cone, and lines of locals every evening. Get a cone and eat it on the bridge at sunset. Unbeatable quantity-quality-price ratio.
places.reviewSummary: Years of student and local loyalty for generous portions at some of the lowest prices of any quality gelateria in town.

quotes.text: A favorite among university students and residents for years... the quality-price ratio is truly unbeatable.

places.name: La Sorbettiera
places.description: An artisan gelateria on quiet Piazza Tasso in San Frediano, famous for 'Catrame' — a dense 75% Peruvian dark-chocolate sorbet — plus perfect peach and hazelnut. Local families and Oltrarno students only; almost no tourists make it out here. Worth the ten-minute detour every time.
places.reviewSummary: Gelato obsessives call the Catrame chocolate sorbet life-changing; consistently ranked at the top of local lists.

quotes.text: A mind-blowing dark chocolate sorbet called Catrame that sends people into absolute ecstasy.

places.name: Gelateria dei Neri
places.description: The classic gelato stop on the All'Antico Vinaio street, with a huge ever-changing case of seasonal flavors — the ricotta-and-fig is the cult order. Cheap, generous and open late, it's the natural dessert after a schiacciata. A genuine local favorite despite the touristy street.
places.reviewSummary: A local meeting point praised for quality ingredients, big flavor range and fair prices on a high-traffic street.

quotes.text: A true meeting place for young people and students of all ages... pistachio and ricotta-fig combinations stand out.
